items.title: jingyaogong/minimind
items.contentSnippet:
🧠 两小时从 0 训出你的 64M 大模型。Train your own 64M LLM from scratch in 2 hours.
https://jingyaogong.github.io/minimind

 
 

 
 
 
 
     
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 
"大道至简"
 
 
 
 
中文 | English
 
 
 
 
此开源项目旨在完全从 0 开始，仅用 3 块钱成本与 2 小时训练时间，即可训练出规模约为 64M 的超小语言模型 MiniMind。
 
 
MiniMind 系列极其轻量，主线最小版本体积约为 GPT-3 的 $\frac{1}{2700}$，力求让普通个人 GPU 也能快速完成训练与复现。
 
 
项目同时开源了大模型的极简结构与完整训练链路，覆盖 MoE、数据清洗、预训练（Pretrain）、监督微调（SFT）、LoRA、RLHF（DPO）、RLAIF（PPO / GRPO / CISPO）、Tool Use、Agentic RL、自适应思考与模型蒸馏等全过程代码。

items.title: Show HN: yavcpdf - A keyboard-driven, vibecoded PDF viewer
items.contentSnippet:
Hi HN,
I wanted a PDF viewer I could drive entirely from the keyboard that could also fill in forms and sign documents.
You might already be acquainted with PDF viewers like zathura and sioyek. This one is similar, except much more performant and not prone to crashes. You can also draw, annotate and fill & sign entirely via keyboard.
It's based off of PdfCraft's (from the ArtCraft project) rendering engine.
The config is configured in TOML and live-reloaded.
Feel free to try and give feedback.

items.title: Show HN: Primeward – Exploring a stateful recurrence for the next prime
items.contentSnippet:
I’ve published Primeward, a Python research prototype. I started with a question: can we calculate the next prime from what we already know, rather than find it by brute force?
The implementation builds on known next-prime formulas. It uses a finite bound and interval arithmetic to extract the exact next prime from a stored arithmetic state, then updates that state and repeats.
It uses the Riemann zeta function and Euler products without assuming the Riemann Hypothesis.
